issue: PROPER discovery sweep for Bolivia (landlocked — checked specifically for any river/virtual-pipeline LNG hub, cross-border export terminal, or Hidrovía LNG facility, per brief). Result: ZERO in-scope LNG terminals, none missing from GEM. Findings: (1) YPFB's Río Grande GNL plant (Cabezas, Santa Cruz) is a DOMESTIC virtual-pipeline / 'gas natural virtual' facility — small-scale liquefaction (210 t/day) feeding cryogenic tanker trucks to satellite regasification stations serving ~27 remote towns. This is gas-by-truck domestic distribution, explicitly the small-scale/out-of-scope category the brief flagged; not a marine import/export terminal. (2) Puerto Busch / Puerto Suárez on the Paraguay-Paraná Hidrovía (transferred to ASP-B Aug 2025, Supreme Decree 5441) is a general cargo/agro-export river port — NO LNG terminal component. (3) The only historical Bolivia LNG EXPORT concept was the 2001 'Pacific LNG' (Margarita field gas liquefied at a Pacific-coast port for US West Coast) — that lineage is the never-built Ilo LNG Terminal already in GEM (Peru side, shelved, YPFB-owned). Bolivian gas output is in steady decline (~31.9 MMcm/d 2025), no new liquefaction/export terminal proposed.
suggested_action: No new_terminal and no monitor entry for Bolivia. The Río Grande GNL plant is intentionally excluded as out-of-scope small-scale virtual-pipeline infrastructure. Re-confirm at a future batch only if Bolivia announces a marine LNG export terminal tied to a Pacific outlet or a Hidrovía LNG-barge export scheme (none exists today).
